guide.title: Germany
guide.body: National proportional allocation determines seats. Regional plurality map colors do not award every seat to that party. The 5% threshold can exclude parties; CSU is exempt. Compatible coalitions can form a government.

guide.title: France
guide.body: Win a majority of presidency points. Six planning weeks compress the two-week runoff. First-round transfers are included in opening support. National broadcasts and platform preparation reach the whole electorate.

guide.title: New Zealand
guide.body: Mixed-member proportional. Seats follow each region's party vote, so a vote gained anywhere counts. The seven Māori electorates form their own pool. Labour and National never govern together; ACT and the Greens pick sides, and NZ First can go either way.

guide.title: Brazil
guide.body: Brazil elects its president in two rounds. You play the runoff, with the first round already counted: the voters of the candidates who lost it (Marina Silva, Ciro Gomes, Simone Tebet and others) are part of the opening map, and events show them moving. Win 51 of 100 points. Each of twelve regions holds points in proportion to the votes cast there, and a region's points go to whoever leads it. The PT is one finalist every time. The Right is the PSDB in 2002, 2006, 2010 and 2014, then Bolsonaro for the PSL (2018) and the PL (2022). The game cannot model the first round itself, so the eliminated candidates' voters cannot be moved through a transfer table. National broadcasts reach everyone, and regional pushes win a region.

guide.title: India
guide.body: First past the post in 543 single-member constituencies, grouped here into fifteen regions. Seats follow each region's vote, so winning a state matters more than winning the country. Parties are the alliances voters faced: the BJP-led NDA and the Congress-led UPA (the INDIA bloc in 2024), with regional parties such as Trinamool, the BJD and the YSRCP shown on their own only where they stood apart from both. Where a regional party was a pre-poll ally, its votes and seats sit with that alliance, so the same party can be inside the NDA in one election and alone in the next. The Lok Sabha needs 272 seats. Congress and the BJP never govern together, and the Samajwadi Party and the Left never join the NDA.

guide.title: Spain
guide.body: 350 seats are won province by province with closed party lists, grouped here into 14 regions. Small provinces mean a party needs a strong local base: the regional parties win seats on a few percent of the national vote, while small national parties win few. A government needs 176 votes in the first investiture ballot, or more yes than no in the second. The game scores the largest party and at most one partner, so real Spanish deals built from several parties and abstentions are reduced to that arithmetic. PP and PSOE never govern together, nobody but the PP deals with Vox, and the Catalan, Basque, Galician and Canarian parties cannot be played but shape every close result.

guide.title: Ireland
guide.body: Single transferable vote in constituencies of three to five seats. The game has no STV count, so each of the ten regions wins seats in line with its first-preference vote, with transfers already folded into the regional seat table, the same shortcut Australia uses for preferences. Independents win a large block of seats and cannot be led. Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael can govern together, but neither will take Sinn Féin, and the Social Democrats, PBP-Solidarity and Aontú will not join either of them.

guide.title: Japan
guide.body: Parallel voting. About 290 seats come from single-member districts and 176 from party lists in eleven regional blocks, and the two tiers do not offset each other. Each block is one region here, and its seats combine its districts and its list seats, so the party that wins a block takes most of them and a swing moves more seats than a pure list system would. The LDP and Komeito govern together by habit. The LDP never partners the Democrats, and the Communists only ever work with the left of the opposition. Chamber size changes: 480 seats in 2009 and 2012, 475 in 2014, 465 since.
